lessons.title: Welcome! What Is Tableau & Course Overview
Downloading and Understanding the Course Datasets

slots.practicalActivity: Install Tableau Desktop (14-day trial) and Tableau Public, then open Desktop and connect to the bundled Sample - Superstore dataset from the start page's Saved Data Sources list. In the Data pane, click through five different fields, noting which sit under Dimensions and which under Measures.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed working Tableau Desktop install with Sample Superstore connected, plus a written list naming three Dimension fields and two Measure fields from memory.

slots.practicalActivity: In the open Superstore workbook, tour every pane (Data, Analytics, the Marks card, Rows/Columns shelves), then drag Category onto Columns and SUM(Sales) onto Rows, and separately drag Order Date onto Columns to compare a blue discrete pill against a green continuous pill.
slots.deliverable: A saved workbook with one worksheet showing a discrete (blue) pill and one showing a continuous (green) pill, plus a one-paragraph note in your own words explaining the difference.

lessons.title: Exercise: Build Your First Tableau Visualization

slots.practicalActivity: Build the course's first-visualization exercise against Sample Superstore from scratch: Category on Columns, SUM(Sales) on Rows, converted to a bar chart, with Region added to Color.
slots.deliverable: A saved workbook file ('01-first-viz.twbx') containing one finished bar chart of Sales by Category, colored by Region.

slots.practicalActivity: Export one sheet of Superstore to both .xlsx and .csv, then reconnect to each via Get Data > Microsoft Excel and Get Data > Text File, comparing the Data Source pane for each. If SQL Server is available, also connect to one table via Get Data > SQL Server; otherwise write out the exact connection steps you'd follow.
slots.deliverable: A workbook with two live connections (Excel and CSV) to the same underlying data, plus a written note on any differences you noticed in the Data Source pane between the two.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Tableau extract (.hyper) from your Superstore connection via Data > Extract Data, compare the connection icon before and after, then manually refresh the extract and inspect Data > Extract > Refresh options.
slots.deliverable: One created and manually refreshed extract, plus a written comparison table of live-connection vs. extract tradeoffs (speed, freshness, portability).

lessons.title: Cleaning Data: Data Interpreter, Splits, Pivots & NULLs

slots.practicalActivity: Build a deliberately messy Excel copy of a Superstore sheet (merged header row, a stray subtotal row), connect to it, turn on Data Interpreter to auto-clean it, then manually fix at least three field data types and split one text column.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned data source with Data Interpreter applied, at least one manually-fixed data type, one split column, and one documented null-handling step.

lessons.title: Wide vs. Long Data & Preparing Data for Tableau

slots.practicalActivity: Build a small wide-format spreadsheet with months as separate columns (Jan Sales, Feb Sales, Mar Sales...), connect to it in Tableau, and use the Data Source pane's pivot feature to reshape it into long format (Month, Sales).
slots.deliverable: A reshaped data source, pivoted from wide to long format, with before/after field lists noted in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, connect to one brand-new public dataset (CSV or Excel) you haven't used in this course, clean it with Data Interpreter, fix at least three field data types, and reshape it to long format if it isn't already.
slots.deliverable: A new, independently cleaned and reshaped data source, built from a dataset not used anywhere else in the course, ready to visualize.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a bar chart of Sales by Sub-Category using the Show Me panel, then build a line chart of Sales by month(Order Date) and convert a copy of it to an area chart.
slots.deliverable: One worksheet with a bar chart built via Show Me and a second worksheet with both a line chart and an area chart variant of the same monthly Sales trend.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a pie chart of Sales by Segment, a tree map of Sales by Category and Sub-Category, a highlight table of Profit by Region and Category, and a heat map of Quantity by State and Category.
slots.deliverable: Four finished worksheets: a pie chart, a tree map, a highlight table, and a heat map, each built from a different field pairing.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a scatter plot of Sales vs. Profit colored by Category and sized by Quantity, then create a bin on Discount (your own bin size) and build a histogram showing the distribution of orders across discount bins.
slots.deliverable: One scatter plot worksheet and one histogram worksheet, with your chosen bin size for Discount noted in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a box-and-whisker plot of Profit by Category to spot outlier orders, then for three different business questions you write yourself (a comparison, a trend, a distribution), pick and justify the chart type that actually answers each one.
slots.deliverable: A box-and-whisker worksheet, plus a written justification naming the right chart type for three self-written business questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Without instructions, rebuild four chart types from this chapter against a field pairing not used in any lesson example (e.g., a tree map of Profit by Region/State instead of Sales by Category/Sub-Category, or a histogram of Quantity instead of Discount).
slots.deliverable: Four original worksheets, each a distinct Chapter 3 chart type, built from field combinations you chose yourself rather than copied from a lesson.

lessons.title: The Marks Card: Color, Size, Detail & Shape

slots.practicalActivity: On an existing bar chart, use the Marks card to color by Sub-Category and size by Profit, add a custom data label, then build a Viz in Tooltip that embeds a small trend line inside the tooltip of a Category-level chart.
slots.deliverable: One worksheet demonstrating Marks-card color and size, plus a working Viz in Tooltip showing an embedded mini-chart on hover.

slots.practicalActivity: Format Sales as currency with no decimals and the Order Date axis to show quarters, then add a dynamic sheet title, a one-line caption, a reference line showing average Sales, and an annotation calling out the single highest-selling point.
slots.deliverable: A polished worksheet with custom number/date formatting, a dynamic title, a reference line, and one annotation, all on the same chart.

slots.practicalActivity: Audit three worksheets you built earlier in this course against a clutter checklist (unnecessary gridlines, redundant legends, inconsistent colors, default titles) and clean each one up.
slots.deliverable: Three earlier worksheets revised for visual cleanliness, with a short written before/after note on what was removed from each.

slots.practicalActivity: Sort Sub-Category bars descending by Sales, add a Category quick filter users can toggle, then build one dimension filter (Segment), one measure filter (Profit > 0), and one date filter (a specific year range) on the same view.
slots.deliverable: One worksheet with sorting, a working quick filter, and at least one each of a dimension, measure, and date filter applied.

lessons.title: Relative Dates, Top N & Conditional Filters

slots.practicalActivity: Add a relative-date filter for the last 12 months of orders, a Top 10 Products by Sales filter, and a conditional filter (Profit greater than zero), then set the date filter as a context filter and compare the Top 10 results before and after.
slots.deliverable: A worksheet with relative-date, Top N, and conditional filters, plus a written before/after note on how making the date filter a context filter changed the Top 10 results.

lessons.title: Analytics Pane: Trend Lines, Forecasting & Reference Lines

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately construct a case where a Top N filter and a context filter interact (Top 10 Products computed before vs. after a Region context filter) to see Tableau's order of operations in action, then drag a trend line and a forecast onto a monthly Sales line chart.
slots.deliverable: A documented order-of-operations example showing the Top 10 results changing based on filter order, plus a chart with both a trend line and a forecast added.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original view combining at least five Chapter 5 techniques without guidance — your own choice of filters, one context filter, and a trend line or forecast — against a dimension/measure pairing you pick yourself.
slots.deliverable: One worksheet demonstrating five or more combined filtering and analytics techniques, with a written note explaining the order they execute in.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Profit Ratio calculated field (SUM([Profit])/SUM([Sales])) and one original KPI calculation of your own choosing, such as Average Order Value, and validate both in a table visual.
slots.deliverable: Two original calculated fields (Profit Ratio and a self-chosen KPI), each validated against a table showing plausible values.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a string calculation that extracts or combines parts of Product Name or Customer Name, and a date calculation using DATEDIFF to compute shipping delay in days between Order Date and Ship Date.
slots.deliverable: One string calculation and one shipping-delay date calculation, both validated against a handful of known rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an IF/THEN/ELSE field classifying orders as High/Medium/Low profit by your own thresholds, rebuild the same logic as a CASE statement, and write a null-handling calculation (IFNULL or ZN) against a deliberately introduced blank value.
slots.deliverable: An IF-based and a CASE-based classification field producing identical results, plus one null-handling calculation tested against a known blank-value row.

lessons.title: Aggregate vs. Non-Aggregate Calculations & Common Errors

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately write a calculation that mixes an aggregate measure with a non-aggregate dimension comparison to trigger Tableau's 'cannot mix aggregate and non-aggregate' error, then fix it.
slots.deliverable: A corrected calculated field, with a written note on the exact error message you triggered and what change resolved it.

slots.practicalActivity: Timed drill: without lesson guidance, write five new calculated fields from scratch in 30 minutes — one arithmetic, one string, one date, one IF/CASE classification, and one null-safe calculation — against fields not used in any lesson example.
slots.deliverable: Five original calculated fields, validated together in one summary table visual.

lessons.title: Dates: Year, Quarter, Month, Week & Day
Continuous vs. Discrete Dates & Time-Series Analysis

slots.practicalActivity: Build the same line chart of Sales over Order Date four times at Year, Quarter, Month, and Week granularity, then toggle each between discrete and continuous to compare the visual difference.
slots.deliverable: Four small line-chart variations by date granularity, plus a written note on when you'd choose discrete vs. continuous dates.

lessons.title: Percent of Total, Difference & Percent Difference

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Percent of Total quick table calculation to a Sales-by-Category view, then write original Difference and Percent Difference table calculations comparing each month's Sales to the previous month.
slots.deliverable: One view with a Percent of Total calculation plus Difference and Percent Difference table calculations, each spot-checked by hand against two adjacent months.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Running Total of monthly Sales and a 3-month Moving Average to one line chart, then build a separate table that ranks every Sub-Category by Profit using the Rank quick table calculation.
slots.deliverable: A line chart with running total and moving average lines, plus a ranked Sub-Category table.

slots.practicalActivity: Take one table calculation from this chapter and manually change its Compute Using setting across Table (Across), Table (Down), and a specific dimension, recording how the output numbers change each time.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison showing the same table calculation's results under three different addressing/partitioning settings, with an explanation of why they differ.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original time-series worksheet combining at least four Chapter 7 techniques without lesson guidance: a chosen date granularity, a running total, a rank calculation, and a deliberately-set Compute Using configuration.
slots.deliverable: One worksheet demonstrating four or more combined time-series/table-calculation techniques, with correct, explainable numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a new data source with two related tables (for example, Orders plus a custom Region lookup table you build in a spreadsheet) using a relationship first, inspecting the logical layer vs. the physical layer in the Data Source pane.
slots.deliverable: A data source with one relationship built between two tables, plus a written note distinguishing Tableau's logical layer from its physical layer.

lessons.title: Creating Joins & Joining on Multiple Fields

slots.practicalActivity: Rebuild the same two tables as a join instead of a relationship, including a multi-field join condition, then deliberately mismatch the join grain (join on a non-unique key) to trigger row duplication, and diagnose the fan-out using SUM totals that are suspiciously too high.
slots.deliverable: A join-based version of the Chapter 8 data source, plus a documented fan-out example showing the inflated totals and the join condition change that fixed it.

slots.practicalActivity: Split a copy of Superstore into two mock date-range extracts and Union them back into one stacked table, then build a blend combining Superstore with a small secondary spreadsheet (e.g. sales targets) on a common field like Region.
slots.deliverable: A unioned combined table confirmed row-complete, plus a separate blended view pulling a measure from a second, independent data source.

lessons.title: Relationships vs. Joins vs. Blending — Which Should You Use?

slots.practicalActivity: For three original scenarios you invent yourself (not the lesson's examples), decide relationship, join, or blend, and write one sentence of justification for each, following the decision process of relationship first, join when something a relationship can't express is needed, and blend as the last resort.
slots.deliverable: A written three-scenario decision log with a justified relationship/join/blend choice for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original data source from scratch combining at least two of this chapter's techniques (for example a relationship plus a union, or a join plus a blend) against tables you choose yourself, without lesson guidance.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-table data source demonstrating at least two combining techniques, with a written rationale for each choice made.

slots.practicalActivity: Confirm or assign geographic roles to State and City, then build a filled map of Sales by State and a separate symbol map of Profit by City.
slots.deliverable: One filled map and one symbol map, both correctly geocoded with no unresolved locations.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately rename one State value (e.g. a typo) to trigger an unresolved-location error on your map, fix it using Edit Locations, then build a custom territory group that combines several States into regions of your own design and color a map by it.
slots.deliverable: A corrected map with zero unresolved locations, plus one custom territory group used to color a second map.

slots.practicalActivity: If a spatial file (a shapefile or GeoJSON of ZIP codes or districts) is available, connect to it in Tableau and layer it onto a map; if not, research and write out the exact Get Data > Spatial File steps you'd follow and what the resulting map layer would show.
slots.deliverable: A map with a spatial data layer added, or a detailed written walkthrough of the spatial-connection steps if no spatial file was available.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a custom group combining several low-volume Sub-Categories into an 'Other' bucket, build a Category > Sub-Category drill-down hierarchy, then create a dynamic set of the Top 10 Customers by Sales that updates as the underlying data changes.
slots.deliverable: One grouped field, one working drill-down hierarchy, and one dynamic set, each demonstrated in its own worksheet.

slots.practicalActivity: Build two sets (Top 10 Customers by Sales, and High-Profit Customers above a threshold you choose), combine them with a Combined Set to see the overlap, then create a bin on Sales and build a histogram that segments customers into value tiers.
slots.deliverable: One Combined Set worksheet showing the union or intersection of two customer sets, and one bin-based customer segmentation histogram.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a string parameter listing Sales, Profit, and Quantity, then wire it into a calculated field (using a CASE on the parameter) that swaps which measure displays on a bar chart when the user changes the parameter.
slots.deliverable: One working parameter-driven calculated field that changes the chart's displayed measure as the parameter value changes.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the previous parameter setup so a second parameter also swaps the dimension on Rows (e.g. Category vs. Region vs. Segment), then build a separate What-If scenario using a numeric discount-rate parameter that recalculates a projected-profit measure live.
slots.deliverable: A worksheet with both swappable measure and dimension via parameters, plus a what-if discount-rate scenario that recalculates projected profit as the parameter changes.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a parameter action so that clicking a mark on one chart (e.g. a Region on a map) updates a parameter, and wire a second calculation to reference that parameter so it visibly updates when you click.
slots.deliverable: A working parameter action, demonstrated by clicking a mark and showing a dependent calculation or highlighted view update in response.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a FIXED LOD field, Customer Lifetime Sales ({ FIXED [Customer Name] : SUM([Sales]) }), and place it on two different views at different levels of detail (e.g. an Order ID-level table and a Region-level summary) to confirm it stays constant per customer regardless of the view.
slots.deliverable: A working FIXED LOD field shown on at least two views at different grains, proving the value stays stable per customer.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an INCLUDE LOD (average Sales per order, included by Order ID, shown on a Category-level view) and an EXCLUDE LOD (a company-wide average that ignores Region), then test how moving a Region filter between a regular filter and a context filter does or doesn't change each result.
slots.deliverable: One INCLUDE and one EXCLUDE LOD field, plus a written note on how a filter's position (regular vs. context) changed, or didn't change, each result and why.

lessons.title: Real-World LOD Analysis: Customer Lifetime Sales & First Purchase

slots.practicalActivity: Follow the lesson's cohort-analysis recipe exactly on Sample Superstore: build Customer Lifetime Sales, Customer First Order Date (both FIXED LOD), a New vs. Returning flag, and a Cohort Month field, then assemble the view (Cohort Month on Rows, AVG(Customer Lifetime Sales) on Columns, filtered to New only).
slots.deliverable: The four-field cohort analysis built end to end, with a written answer naming which cohort month has the highest average lifetime value.

slots.practicalActivity: Design one original LOD-based analysis for a business question you invent yourself (not the cohort scenario), using at least one FIXED expression and one INCLUDE or EXCLUDE expression, without lesson guidance.
slots.deliverable: Two or more original LOD fields answering a self-chosen business question in one finished view, with a written explanation of why a table calculation couldn't do the same job.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a dual-axis combo chart with Sales as bars and Profit Ratio as a synchronized line, then build a KPI card showing a single metric with a small embedded sparkline trend beside it.
slots.deliverable: One dual-axis combo chart with synchronized axes, and one KPI card with an embedded sparkline.

lessons.title: Advanced Reference Lines, Bands & Dynamic Targets

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Pareto chart of Sales by Sub-Category with a cumulative-percentage line, then add a dynamic reference band to a different chart that's driven by a parameter representing a target you can adjust.
slots.deliverable: A Pareto chart with a working cumulative-percent line, plus a chart with a dynamic reference band tied to a parameter.

slots.practicalActivity: Complete the course's Advanced Chart Challenge independently: pick one advanced chart type from this chapter and build it against a business question you define yourself, not copied from a lesson example.
slots.deliverable: One finished advanced-chart-challenge worksheet, with a written statement of the specific business question it answers.

lessons.title: Dashboard Layout: Containers, Tiled & Floating Objects

slots.practicalActivity: Following the lesson's five-step build order (finish worksheets, set size, place the anchor view, add supporting views, add KPI header last), assemble a dashboard from three finished worksheets with a Range size (minimum 800x600, maximum 1400x900), then rework spacing using tiled containers and one floating object.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard with a Range size, built via the five-step order, using at least one tiled container and one floating object.

lessons.title: Building KPI Headers & Executive Summary Sections

slots.practicalActivity: Add a KPI header row across the top of the dashboard (Total Sales, Total Profit, Profit Ratio), then wire a filter action so clicking a Region filters the other sheets, and a separate highlight action on a different field.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard with a working KPI header plus one filter action and one highlight action, both verified by clicking through in Presentation Mode.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a URL action linking a selected mark to a web address, a parameter or set action triggered by selection, a navigation button to a second dashboard page, a show/hide container toggle, and a dynamic title that changes with the current selection.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard with a URL action, a parameter or set action, a navigation button, a show/hide toggle, and a dynamic title, each tested by clicking through.

slots.practicalActivity: Use Device Designer to add a phone-specific layout to the dashboard, write a one-paragraph 'how to read this' caption aimed at a first-time viewer, then run the Performance Recorder and note any slow-loading sheet or query.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard with a device-specific phone layout, a reader-facing caption, and a written performance note identifying the slowest element from the Performance Recorder.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, build one original one-page dashboard combining at least four Chapter 14 techniques — a KPI header, one filter or highlight action, one navigation or show/hide element, and a dynamic title — against a business question of your own choosing. (Save the Executive Sales Dashboard itself for Chapter 17's dedicated project.)
slots.deliverable: One original, fully interactive one-page dashboard demonstrating four or more Chapter 14 techniques, built from a self-chosen business question.

lessons.title: Tableau Desktop vs. Public vs. Cloud vs. Server

slots.practicalActivity: Write a comparison of Desktop vs. Public vs. Cloud vs. Server (who hosts it, who sees it, approximate cost), then publish one of your Chapter 14 dashboards to Tableau Public (or a Tableau Cloud trial if you have access).
slots.deliverable: A written four-way comparison of Desktop/Public/Cloud/Server, plus a dashboard live on Tableau Public or Cloud with a shareable link.

slots.practicalActivity: On your published workbook, configure (or if unavailable, document step by step) viewer permissions, an extract refresh schedule, and a subscription that emails the view on a recurring basis.
slots.deliverable: A documented permissions, refresh, and subscription configuration for the published workbook, including confirmation that a subscription was set up successfully.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the Performance Recorder against one of your dashboards, identify the slowest sheet or query, then apply at least two concrete optimizations (switching to an extract, hiding unused fields, simplifying a calculation, or reducing marks), and re-record to confirm the improvement.
slots.deliverable: A before-and-after Performance Recorder comparison showing a measurable improvement after applying two or more optimizations.

slots.practicalActivity: Build Project 1 against Sample Superstore exactly to spec: a Profit Ratio calculated field, a KPI header (Total Sales, Total Profit, Profit Ratio), a sales-by-region map colored by Profit Ratio, a profit-trend line chart with a reference line, a Top 10 products bar chart built with an actual Top N filter, and a working filter action linking the map to the trend and Top 10 charts.
slots.deliverable: Project 1 built end to end and checked against every row of the project rubric: KPI header, map, trend chart, Top 10 chart, filter action, one-screen layout, and framing.

slots.practicalActivity: Continue and polish Project 1: verify the filter action works reliably in Presentation Mode, clean up fonts/colors/titles so nothing looks like a Tableau default, and write the dashboard's one-line 'how to read this' caption.
slots.deliverable: Project 1 fully polished, passing every row of its rubric, with a finished title and caption.

slots.practicalActivity: Build Project 2, a customer segmentation dashboard: segment customers using a set or bin from Chapter 10 (e.g. high-value vs. low-value customers, or new vs. returning via the Chapter 12 LOD fields), and visualize segment-level Sales and Profit using at least one LOD-based calculation.
slots.deliverable: A finished customer segmentation dashboard combining at least one set or group technique with one LOD expression.

slots.practicalActivity: Continue and polish Project 2: add interactivity letting the viewer switch between segmentation views (a parameter or filter action), and review it against the same quality bar used for Project 1 — consistent formatting, working interactivity, and a clear framing caption.
slots.deliverable: Project 2 fully polished with working interactivity and a finished framing caption.

slots.practicalActivity: Build Project 3, an enterprise performance dashboard combining a multi-table data model from Chapter 8 (a relationship or join across at least two tables) with a time-series table calculation from Chapter 7 (e.g. a running total or year-over-year comparison) and at least one dashboard action from Chapter 14.
slots.deliverable: A finished enterprise performance dashboard built on a multi-table data model, including one time-series table calculation and one dashboard action.

slots.practicalActivity: Using your three finished portfolio dashboards, write a one-paragraph case-study description for each (business question, approach, outcome), then rehearse a 5-minute walkthrough of your strongest dashboard as if presenting to an interviewer.
slots.deliverable: Three written case-study blurbs, one per project, plus rehearsed notes for a 5-minute interview walkthrough of your best dashboard.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can independently connect to and model real business data in Tableau, build calculated fields, time-intelligence table calculations, and Level of Detail expressions, and design, publish, and present polished, interactive Tableau dashboards end to end.
